images.title: Ten dots, two shapes
images.purpose: Show that the same 10 dots make a triangle and a rectangle.
images.composition: Two dot groups side by side with a wide gap, a sum under each, centred.
images.exact_structure: Left: 10 equal dots in a triangle of rows of 1, 2, 3 and 4 dots, in teal #0072B2. Right: 10 equal dots of the same size in a rectangle of 2 rows of 5 dots, in amber #E69F00. Dots evenly spaced. Exactly 2 groups, 20 dots drawn in all.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a group with other than 10 dots
images.takeaway: The same number of dots can be arranged in different shapes.
images.description: A triangle of 10 dots beside a rectangle of 2 rows of 5 dots.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the dots in each group and say what is the same and what differs.

image_decisions.why: Two groups with matching counts show same dots, different shape.
